sources.citation: Buecher, Segers and Staud, Consistency of M-estimators for non-identically distributed data: the case of fixed-design distributional regression
sources.observed_version: HTML identifies arXiv:2511.11067v1; title page gives August 24, 2026
sources.sections_read: Introduction, Assumptions 1-5, Theorem 2.2, and beginning of Section 3 including Assumption 6
sources.theorem_scope: Theorem 2.2 assumes rowwise independence, convergence of averaged observation laws, compact parameter space, upper-semicontinuous criterion, unique finite population maximum, continuity at the true parameter, and local uniform integrability; approximate criterion maximizers are weakly consistent.
sources.applicability: Exact replication preserves the average law and the stated integrability assumptions. These sufficient assumptions do not follow from original M-estimator consistency for an arbitrary fixed nested design; compactness/global population identification are additional obligations. The result is therefore not a solution of the broad target.

sources.citation: Liese and Vajda (2003), On sqrt(n)-Consistency and Asymptotic Normality of Consistent Estimators in Models with Independent Observations, Rostocker Mathematisches Kolloquium 57, 3-51
sources.sections_read: Printed pp. 3-11, including Definition 2.1, Theorems 2.2-2.3 and R1-R4+
sources.applicability: Definition 2.1 already assumes weak consistency for an adapted estimator. Theorem 2.2 then establishes a rate under uniformly bounded locator gradients, nondegenerate normalized design limits and score regularity. Applying it to the pooled estimator would assume the conclusion sought. It is not used to justify pooled consistency.
